links.outcome: Accuracy of automated hallucination and omission detection in mental health chatbot responses, LLM judges versus expert-informed features
links.effect: LLM judges reached only 52% accuracy, with some near-zero recall. Expert-informed feature models reached 0.717 F1 (custom dataset) and 0.849 F1 (public benchmark) for hallucinations, and 0.59-0.64 F1 for omissions.
links.quote: We show that leading LLM judges achieve only 52% accuracy on mental health counseling data, with some hallucination detection approaches exhibiting near-zero recall.

unlisted_practices: Combining human expertise with LLMs to extract interpretable features (logical consistency, entity verification, factual accuracy, linguistic uncertainty, professional appropriateness) for hallucination and omission detection

screen.reason: Evaluates a domain-informed guardrail framework blending human expertise with automated extraction to detect hallucinations and omissions in mental health chatbot outputs.
